_notes._history: tabs.create:resolve used to be allowlisted here for the native Chrome-vs-Firefox tabs.Tab shape difference (Chrome-only: selected, frozen; Firefox-only: attention, hidden, isArticle, isInReaderMode, sharingState, successorTabId, cookieStoreId). Fixed properly in diff.ts's normalizeTrace instead: any Tab-shaped object (id+windowId+index+boolean active) is now projected down to {url, title, status, index, active} before comparison, so that entire class of divergence is gone.
_notes.tabs.create:resolve: Much smaller residual after the shape-projection fix: verified via re-run that the ONLY remaining difference is the `status` field (chrome: "loading", firefox: "complete") -- both sides otherwise now normalize identically (index, active match; url/title absent on both, matching this extension's permission scope). This is a genuine browser-native timing race in when each engine resolves the tabs.create() promise relative to the new tab's initial paint, not extension or converter behavior, and not fixable by adjusting probe delays (the capture happens synchronously in the shim's promise-then hook, with no artificial wait in between).

extensions.name: OneNote Web Clipper

_notes._offscreen_cascade_root_cause: OneNote's background script (minified from build/scripts/communicator/offscreenCommunicator.js) calls chrome.runtime.getContexts({contextTypes:[chrome.runtime.ContextType.OFFSCREEN_DOCUMENT], ...}) unconditionally, with no chrome.offscreen feature-detection guard. On Firefox, chrome.runtime.ContextType.OFFSCREEN_DOCUMENT is undefined (Firefox has no offscreen-document context type), so the call becomes getContexts({contextTypes:[undefined]}), which Firefox's WebExtensions API rejects synchronously ('Expected string instead of undefined'). The extension gates its entire post-install setup behind that same promise (clipperIdProcessed) via bare .then() with no .catch() anywhere (registerContextMenuItems(), onInstalled(), and invokeClipperInTab()'s actual clip-trigger path all chain off it), so on Firefox none of it ever runs: no offscreen document, no context menus, no 'getting started' tour tab, no translated-strings fetch, no clipperId relay -- and clipping itself silently never fires. This is a bug in OneNote's own source (unconditional use of a Chrome-only API), not a chrome2moz mis-conversion; filed as a converter-enhancement candidate at https://github.com/OtsoBear/chrome2moz/issues/2. All patterns below except management.uninstallSelf* are consequences of this single root cause.
_notes.offscreen.*: See _offscreen_cascade_root_cause. Firefox never reaches offscreen.createDocument at all (aborts earlier at getContexts), so this is chrome-only in the trace.
_notes.runtime.getContexts*: See _offscreen_cascade_root_cause. Covers runtime.getContexts / :resolve (chrome, succeeds) and :throw (firefox, the synchronous TypeError).
_notes.runtime.error#for runtime.getContexts: See _offscreen_cascade_root_cause -- the same getContexts TypeError also surfaces via the shim's global error/unhandledrejection listeners. Pinned to the observed message substring ('...for runtime.getContexts.') via the api#substring allowlist form, so an unrelated runtime.error for this extension is NOT masked.
_notes.runtime.sendMessage#offscreen: See _offscreen_cascade_root_cause -- all chrome-only calls carry target:"offscreen" payloads (clipperId read/set/remove relay to the offscreen document), never reached on Firefox. Pinned to the substring "offscreen" via api#substring so OneNote's other runtime.sendMessage call sites (contentCaptureInject.js, logManager.js, regionOverlay.js -- the actual clip flow, not currently probed) are NOT masked if probes are later extended to exercise them.
_notes.runtime.getManifest: See _offscreen_cascade_root_cause -- called from within the gated onInstalled() setup (chrome-only in the trace). Left name-only (not pinned): OneNote calls getManifest with no arguments, so there's no argument substring to pin to, and the API has no other call sites in this extension.
_notes.net.fetch#onenote.com/strings: See _offscreen_cascade_root_cause -- pinned to the exact observed URL (GET https://www.onenote.com/strings?... -- localized UI strings for the getting-started tour/context menu), fetched only from within the gated onInstalled() path. A net.fetch divergence to any other URL is NOT masked.
_notes.tabs.query#lastFocusedWindow: See _offscreen_cascade_root_cause -- used to find the active tab for the getting-started tour ({active:true, lastFocusedWindow:true}), inside the gated onInstalled() path. Pinned to "lastFocusedWindow" via api#substring; Call args only (a query filter object, not a Tab result), so the Tab-shape normalizer fix doesn't apply here -- Firefox simply never reaches this call at all.
_notes.tabs.create#getting-started: See _offscreen_cascade_root_cause -- opens the getting-started tour tab (support.microsoft.com/.../getting-started-with-the-onenote-web-clipper-...), inside the gated onInstalled() path; never called on Firefox at all (not a shape difference -- the call itself doesn't happen), so the Tab-shape normalizer can't help here. Pinned to "getting-started" via api#substring.
_notes.tabs.create:resolve: Verified via re-run (post shape-projection fix, and after gating pingProbe -- see below -- eliminated the unrelated fixture-tab source this used to also cover) this is now ONLY the offscreen-cascade tour tab, chrome-only: Firefox never calls tabs.create for it at all (zero events on that side, not a shape or timing mismatch). Left name-only (not pinned): at resolve time the tab's url/title are still empty ({url:"",title:"",status:"loading",...} -- the promise resolves before navigation starts), so there is no distinctive substring to pin to yet. Distinct from latextocalc's tabs.create:resolve allowance, which is a real cross-browser timing race present on BOTH sides.
_notes.tabs.onCreated:fired: Verified via re-run this is now ONLY the offscreen-cascade tour tab, chrome-only -- the same fixture-tab source it used to also cover (OneNote's own tabs.onCreated/onUpdated listener, registerTabCreateOrUpdateListener in chromeExtension.js, observing the harness's probe-driven page-opens) is gone now that pingProbe skips opening any page when content_scripts can't cover the fixture origin (see pingProbe note below), instead of opening one anyway. Left name-only (not pinned): onCreated's snapshot is {url:"",title:"",status:"loading",index:1,active:true} -- empty url/title, no distinctive substring available (the tab hasn't started navigating yet when onCreated fires).
_notes.tabs.onUpdated:fired#getting-started: Same source as tabs.onCreated:fired above (the tour tab's own navigation, chrome-only) -- also now free of the fixture-tab noise it used to carry (see tabs.onCreated:fired note and pingProbe note below). Every remaining event's changeInfo/tab carries the tour tab's URL once navigation starts, so pinned to "getting-started" via api#substring. NOTE: an earlier version of this note incorrectly attributed most of these events to a permanent Chrome-vs-Firefox tabs.onUpdated changeInfo-shape difference (citing Firefox-only Reader-Mode isArticle updates on the harness's own fixture tab) -- that was real but was the FIXTURE-tab source, now eliminated by the pingProbe gating fix below, not an unreconcilable difference in the tour-tab source that remains here.
_notes.pingProbe (harness fix, not an allowed_d: probes.ts's pingProbe now checks contentScriptsCoverUrl(manifest, fixtureUrl) BEFORE opening any pages (same check contentProbe already used), skipping immediately when content_scripts can't cover the fixture origin -- which is OneNote's case (content_scripts only match onenote.officeapps.live.com). Previously it opened pages regardless and only recognized the no-content-script case afterward, which meant OneNote's own tabs.onCreated/onUpdated listener observed the harness's probe-driven fixture tab and produced a second, unrelated source of tabs.onCreated:fired/tabs.onUpdated:fired divergence tangled up with the tour-tab (offscreen-cascade) one. Gating removed that second source entirely, roughly halving the residual divergence count and leaving only the tour-tab source documented above.
_notes.contextMenus.*: See _offscreen_cascade_root_cause -- contextMenus.create (one per clip action) and contextMenus.removeAll are called from registerContextMenuItems(), itself gated behind the same clipperIdProcessed promise; never runs on Firefox.
_notes.management.uninstallSelf*: Kept from the original task spec as a defensive/regression-guard pattern. Investigated: this pinned version (3.11.2) does not declare the `management` permission at all and never calls management.uninstallSelf in either trace, so the pattern is currently inert (matches nothing). Left in place in case a future re-pin reintroduces browser-detection + self-uninstall behavior, per the binding decision that this entry exists partly to catch that regression.

extensions._note: gates nothing until a fixture host matching its content_scripts (onenote.officeapps.live.com) exists -- tracked in issue #5

_notes.offscreen.*: Firefox-side offscreen.* calls hit the converter's polyfill, which is injected AFTER the spy shim walks the API surface (issue #6) -- so they are untraced on that side and appear chrome-only (offscreen.createDocument / :resolve). Behavioral equivalence is asserted by the storage.local.set offscreenResult write, which must match on both sides.
_notes.runtime.getContexts*: Same issue #6 root cause, one layer deeper than expected: the polyfill's getContexts wrapper replaces chrome.runtime.getContexts directly (shims/offscreen-polyfill.js), so on Firefox the call never reaches the spy-wrapped original at all when the extension's contextTypes filter is exactly [OFFSCREEN_DOCUMENT] -- the wrapper intentionally skips calling through to the real getContexts in that case (an empty contextTypes array matches everything in the native API, so it must never be passed through). Verified via trace inspection this is a tracing gap, not a functional one: Chrome's real getContexts call resolves to [] (no offscreen doc registered yet) and the extension proceeds identically on both sides.
_notes.runtime.getURL#offscreen.html: The polyfill's offscreen.createDocument implementation calls rt.getURL(url) itself (to resolve the iframe src), in addition to the extension's own t.getURL("offscreen.html") call -- so Firefox observes one extra runtime.getURL call the spy shim did capture (this one runs through the untouched original, unlike getContexts above). Pinned to the literal URL since this extension has only one; a runtime.getURL divergence for any other URL is NOT masked.
